KR.read: Korea's men's grooming segment retains its Euromonitor anchor, though a new same-institution figure now conflicts with it: Euromonitor-via-Korea-Herald puts men's cosmetics at KRW 1.16tn (~US$0.78bn) for CY2025, MEDIUM confidence, RETAIL basis, while a separately-sourced Euromonitor-via-AMPM figure puts 2024 at KRW 1.2tn (~US$0.81bn) — a higher value for an earlier year from what appears to be the same underlying series, an unreconciled internal contradiction (one vintage is likely misdated or the category was rebased); do not build a growth rate across the two. A separate Future Market Insights estimate puts men's SKINCARE alone at US$1.2bn (2025, LOW) — still implausibly exceeding the whole men's-cosmetics figure, the same definitional mismatch as before.
KR.trend: A cleaner same-series growth read is now available: Euromonitor-via-Jangup-Shinmun figures for 2020-2022 (KRW 1.064tn to 1.0751tn to 1.0923tn) imply +1.04% (2021) and +1.6% (2022) YoY (both ESTIMATE confidence, derived) — the 2022 figure cross-validates the KRW 1.09tn (2022) point already on file, confirming the series. The substantive finding: Korean domestic men's cosmetics is growing only around 1-2%/year in nominal KRW (flat-to-negative in real terms against Korean CPI) — well below both the 'booming K-male grooming' narrative and Future Market Insights' 11.04% CAGR forecast (2025-2035, LOW, on the men's-skincare-only basket, not the whole segment).
KR.caveats: The one reasonably-solid figure (Euromonitor, MEDIUM) covers 'men's cosmetics', but two Euromonitor-attributed vintages now conflict (KRW 1.16tn for 2025 vs KRW 1.2tn for 2024) and are not reconciled, so absolute scale should be read as anchored in the low-single-digit KRW trillions but not pinned to either exact figure; the LOW FMI figure uses a broader, internally-inconsistent skincare basket that exceeds both. The firmer signal is the ~1-2%/year nominal growth rate (ESTIMATE, derived from a consistent 2020-2022 series).

IN.read: India men's grooming is the better-evidenced side: Euromonitor sizes it at INR 186.3bn (~US$1.94bn) for 2025, HIGH confidence, RETAIL, growing +9% YoY (also HIGH). IBEF frames the trajectory as INR 20,500cr (2024) to INR 38,300cr (2033), MEDIUM. The men's_skincare sub-segment — corridor whitespace #4 — sizes ~US$1.02bn (Deep Market Insights, LOW). Several LOW aggregator whole-segment estimates cluster US$2.3-2.45bn on differing 'male grooming' baskets.
IN.trend: Observed +9% YoY for 2025 (HIGH, Euromonitor). Forecast CAGRs span 5-12% (LOW-MEDIUM) depending on basket; IBEF's 2024-2033 path implies roughly 7%. Men's skincare is repeatedly cited as the fastest-growing slice, consistent with the whitespace read, though the sub-segment growth figures themselves are LOW.
IN.caveats: Only the Euromonitor size and growth are HIGH confidence; the aggregator estimates vary materially in scope (men's cosmetics vs 'male grooming products' vs razors-inclusive), so they corroborate direction, not a precise number.

combined.read: Both sides now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional comparison holds: India (~US$1.94bn, HIGH, 2025) is roughly 2.5x the size of Korea's men's cosmetics (~US$0.78bn, MEDIUM, 2025) in absolute terms and is far better evidenced. The confidence gap matters — India's figure is Euromonitor-HIGH, Korea's is Euromonitor-MEDIUM via press — so treat the ratio as directional. Korea's distinction is intensity, not size: it is the world's highest per-capita men's beauty market, whereas India is the larger absolute opportunity with men's skincare flagged as corridor whitespace. No K-beauty men's-grooming-in-India market figure surfaced in research, so the corridor angle here stays qualitative.
